author: agent
text: measured on synthetic boards at 70, 700 and 2000 tasks — render goes 0.04s to 0.08s to 0.16s and context 0.04s to 0.07s to 0.18s, so removing all 500 closed tasks from the 2000-task board saves 50ms on render and 70ms on context; the performance argument for relocating closed tasks does not exist at any board size a person will reach

author: agent
text: closed tasks own 3006 of 4520 page lines at 2000 tasks, 66 percent — but every one of those lines is inside the closed details fold, which a git host renders as a single collapsed line, so relocating them removes roughly zero visible lines while the open table stays 1500 rows either way

author: agent
text: GitHub renders markdown only up to 512 KB and cuts a larger README off at exactly 512000 bytes rather than refusing it, so an oversized board page displays as a complete one that silently stops — the page measures 314 bytes per task, which puts the cliff at about 1670 tasks, roughly two years at the rate next.scrapcycle.org is accumulating them
mechanism: GitHub truncates rather than errors, so the failure is invisible on the page itself

author: agent
text: moving closed tasks to a .done folder does not fix the 512 KB cliff because it only divides page growth by three, pushing the cliff from about 1670 tasks to about 5000 while leaving it linear — the page still grows without bound and still truncates silently, just later, and the cost is that taskDir, taskPath and logPath stop being pure joins
mechanism: relocation changes the constant on linear growth; only a cap makes the page constant-size

author: agent
text: cap the closed section and the open table the way DEAD_END_CAP and QUESTION_CAP already cap theirs, rather than relocate closed tasks, because a cap bounds the page at constant size while a folder move only delays an unbounded one — render.ts already carries the convention and the comment that every cap must announce itself on the page, and cairn search reaches everything a cap hides

author: agent
text: compaction is not doing the job DESIGN.md section 7 assigns it — on scrapcycle a closed task.md averages 1428 bytes against 1568 for an open one, so closing a task barely shrinks it, and the done --compact path only moves Context into the log when it exceeds 200 characters
